# Minecraft 1.21.1 kernel oracle

`minecraft-1.21.1-kernels.jsonl` was produced by `VanillaKernelReference.java`
using the project's mapped Minecraft 1.21.1 classes on Oracle JDK 21.0.6.
Regenerate with `gradle --offline -I tools/rust/reference.gradle captureVanillaKernels`.

The oracle invokes Minecraft's `LegacyRandomSource`, `XoroshiroRandomSource`,
`WorldgenRandom`, `ImprovedNoise`, `SimplexNoise`, `PerlinNoise`, and `NormalNoise`.
It does not call the new Rust library or a hand-translated Java algorithm.
Raw long values are decimal strings; expected double values are unsigned raw
64-bit hexadecimal strings. Input decimal coordinates require correctly rounded
JSON parsing (`serde_json` feature `float_roundtrip`).

Seven seeds include zero, signed extrema and the user's two captured world seeds.
Cases cover sequential mixed random methods, rejection bounds, positional and
UTF-8/UTF-16 name derivation, decoration/feature seeds, negative/border/large
coordinates, zero/sparse amplitudes, modern and legacy octaves, and Y scaling.
308 JSON lines give 97,440 exact comparisons. The file is a numeric oracle,
not a complete terrain, biome, surface-rule or vegetation acceptance suite.

`minecraft-1.21.1-noise-dependencies.jsonl` is generated by
`VanillaNoiseDependencyReference.java`, using
`gradle --offline -I tools/rust/reference.gradle referenceVanillaNoiseDependencies`.
It calls the same original classes plus BlendedNoise, PerlinSimplexNoise,
ImprovedNoise.noiseWithDerivative and nextGaussian. Its 252 rows cover the
three dimension presets, RandomState terrain seed derivation, positive/negative
and sparse Simplex octaves, accumulating derivatives and Gaussian reseeding.
No world capture or native library is read by this generator.

56,014 non-Gaussian checks are bit exact. Gaussian comparisons have an explicit
4-ULP bound for Java/platform logarithm and square root rounding, while following
the stream consumption and cache states exactly. On the measured Windows x64
run 7,167 of 7,168 Gaussians were exact and the maximum difference was 1 ULP.
This is a reported limit, not a claim of cross-platform feature equivalence.

## Minecraft 26.3 references

`worldgen263` is a separate set generated with Java 25 and the actual Minecraft
26.3 classes. It does not reinterpret the legacy 1.21.1 fixtures as modern data.
The portable exporters are `tools/verification/Minecraft263NativeReference.java`
and `tools/verification/Minecraft263VegetationReference.java` in the repository.
They use the corresponding compiled Java test runtime and actual registries.

The overworld, Nether and End files contain float density and complete base
column references across three seeds, negative and distant coordinates, bulk
queries, partial height ranges and differing cell sizes. `beard.json` contains
the original structure contribution results, including piece and junction data.

`features.json` uses the production snapshot corrections and complete block
definitions, provider registries, placed features and actual block tags.
`providers.jsonl` contains 960 optional/state/RNG comparisons;
`vegetation.jsonl` contains 176 Nether feature cases; `modern.jsonl` contains
496 composition and boundary cases; `trees263.jsonl` contains 80 tree/mushroom
cases. The two state palettes are independent. Complete final states and the
next random long are checked, including obstructions, null providers, column
truncation, zero-length pillars and sequence/overlay evaluation order.

The CherryFoliagePlacer codec exports its corner probability using the wrong
getter. These fixtures apply `VanillaFeatureSnapshot.correct`, exactly as the
production server snapshot does, while the expected placement still calls the
unmodified original Minecraft feature implementation.
